why: Dynamic keys (plan 2026-10-28 section 4). A literal key on a Record<string, T> dictionary is a map read: an owned key its value, a missing key undefined, an Object.prototype name a value of that name. limitOf rewrites `v === undefined ? 0 : v` as `?? 0` (proved). pageOf reads another key (unproved; lane B WITNESS when page and size differ). A computed string key written with a null value is read when a test against '__proto__' rules that name out before the write: putItem moves the guard from `if (k !== '__proto__')` to an early return on `k === '__proto__'` (proved); putChecked writes 0 where the parent wrote null (unproved; WITNESS). acceptOf reads a declared field of a record that also has an index signature, untouched (proved). An undeclared key of that record stays refused (escape dynamic_key_index_signature), an unguarded object or null write under a string key stays refused (escape proto_write_object, rule prototype), a computed key on a declared record holding a method stays refused (escape dynamic_key_record_member).
